svg.aria-label: Three panels. Top: the cable modelled as a ladder of axial resistors along the core with resistor-capacitor branches to ground, showing injected current choosing between flowing down the core and leaking across the membrane. Middle: steady-state voltage decaying exponentially with distance for a thin and a thick fibre, with the one-over-e points marked, showing that ten times the diameter buys only about three times the reach. Bottom: a myelinated axon whose spike decays slightly between nodes of Ranvier and is regenerated to full amplitude at each node, contrasted with an unmyelinated fibre in which the same signal dies within a fraction of the distance.
svg.text: Cable theory: the current’s two paths, the length constant, and saltatory conduction
(a) The cable as a ladder: axial resistance along the core, an RC patch to ground at every point
(2) or out across the membrane — that competition is the whole theory
(b) Steady injection at x = 0: the voltage decays exponentially, with reach set by λ
(c) Myelinated axon: slight passive decay across each internode, full regeneration at each node
the same axon unmyelinated: gone in half a millimetre
Assumed throughout: Rᵢ = 100 Ω·cm, Rₘ = 10⁴ Ω·cm², Cₘ = 1 µF/cm².
